title: Consors Finanz BNP Paribas is always at hand!
description: Thanks to the Consors Finanz App you always know what dreams are within your reach. Plus, you can always choose whether you prefer to pay off your Mastercard purchases with one-time quarterly payments or in monthly instalments.  For more information: https://www.consorsfinanz.de/

asr.full_text: Caes the moment. The Consosfinance Mastercard is always at hand. and with our app you have everything at your finger tips including your real time account balance and all transactions. Now is the right time to make a wish come true. Thanks to the ConsosFinance App you always know what dreams are within your reach. Plus, you can always choose whether you prefer to pay off your purchases with one-time quarterly payments or in monthly installments for the perfect shopping experience – at home and away. Pay for your purchases with Consos Finance and receive immediate push notifications. The repayment options for your purchases are presented clearly and you can flexibly select the installment amount at all times. Installments up, Installments down… you have the freedom. While Face-ID, Fingerprint and SMS TAN codes guarantee maximum security. Download the app now – Consosfinance.de slash mobilebanking By the way, with your MasterCard all withdrawals above three hundred euros are free of charge worldwide.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it promotes a Consors Finanz BNP Paribas Mastercard-linked mobile banking app with account viewing, transaction monitoring, repayment choices, and flexible installments. The app download and repayment encouragement are presented as ordinary branded banking functionality, without an unusually easy wealth claim, credential-harvesting request, impersonation setup, or deceptive outcome.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary content is an ordinary branded financial service promotion involving a Mastercard, mobile account and transaction viewing, and purchase installment options. The supplied evidence does not establish a scam mechanism.
